headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: nullclaw’s writable workspace and broad egress can collide with gpt-researcher’s file-reading, browser, and MCP-driven research pipeline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and calls MCP; nullclaw exposes webhooks, agent-card, ws, and MCP-like channels. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if nullclaw forwards untrusted content into gpt-researcher’s research inputs. The exact bridge is undocumented, so I avoid high, but the interaction is credible for both agents.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards webhook, ws, or agent-card content into gpt-researcher prompts or MCP calls
IF gpt-researcher treats retrieved web or file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding from nullclaw webhooks to gpt-researcher prompts
Require provenance tags on all content passed between agents
Add a fixed allowlist of MCP tools for the pair
Insert a human review step before executing instructions extracted from web content
requires-engineering: sandbox and schema-validate all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch sensitive classes and have broad network egress; nullclaw explicitly handles keys, tokens, and workspace files, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends research through external APIs. If they share a workspace or hand off files, secrets can flow from nullclaw into gpt-researcher’s outbound requests, creating exfiltration risk in default-style research workflows.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace or mounted files
IF nullclaw stores tokens or private keys in files that gpt-researcher can read
IF gpt-researcher sends those files or derived context to external APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount only read-only inputs to gpt-researcher
Move secrets out of shared files before running either agent
Block outbound requests from gpt-researcher on secret-bearing paths
Rotate any credentials already present in shared directories
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before outbound API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write files, modify git state, and use broad egress; gpt-researcher can read files, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and browse. If they operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF nullclaw writes while gpt-researcher is reading or publishing
IF no external lock or queue serializes file and git operations
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Serialize git writes through one designated actor
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Run one agent in read-only mode for shared repos
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher’s planner/execution/publisher flow can turn upstream outputs into polished reports, while nullclaw’s webhook and scheduling surfaces can feed it operational inputs. That makes a mistaken or manipulated output from one agent likely to propagate into the other’s downstream actions, but the profiles do not show fully autonomous irreversible actions, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF nullclaw passes generated text or webhook payloads directly into gpt-researcher reports
IF gpt-researcher publishes outputs without a verification step
IF downstream consumers treat the published report as authoritative
mitigations: Require citation checks before publishing research outputs
Add a second-pass verifier for any cross-agent handoff
Mark inter-agent content as untrusted by default
Limit nullclaw-triggered tasks to draft mode
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware review gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles handle sensitive data classes, but only nullclaw explicitly lists tokens, private keys, and audit logs, while gpt-researcher lists research documents and citations. The pair can therefore create retention and handling mismatches if the same data class is routed through both systems. No residency or certification details are provided, so I cannot justify high.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher inputs or nullclaw workspace files
IF one agent retains logs or memory longer than the other
IF deletion or export requests must cover both agents' stored copies
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Set short retention on logs and memory for both agents
Document which agent stores each data class
Purge secrets from nullclaw before research runs
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
